criteria.evidence: "In: the list of types the plays need, each with its one-line meaning: Business Intent, Epic, Story, Bug, Chore, Spike." and "Out: a record of what was made and what was mapped." The six one-line meanings the brief must show are never given, and the record has no named place. Rules & behavior covers yes, no, all-present and cannot-make, but not these branches: the product owner approves only some of the missing types; making a type fails (for example the account lacks the rights to add an organization-level type on GitHub); initialize runs again when a mapping already exists.
criteria.fix: In Inputs / Outputs, write the one-line meaning of each of the six types (for example "Spike: a time-boxed look into an unknown, with a finding as its result") and name where the record is kept (for example beside the mapping in the project's settings). In Rules & behavior, add one line each for: a partial yes (make only the approved types; the rest stay missing and are named in the brief); a make that fails (say what failed in plain words, make nothing further for that type, leave it unmapped so plays stop with the initialize message); and a run where a mapping already exists (keep it, show it in the brief, and change it only on a new yes), pointing to fn-rerun-initialize for the rest of the re-run.

criteria.evidence: "Nothing is made in the tracker before the product owner's typed yes. A tracker is an outside system, and a new type there is seen by the whole team."; "GitHub works first. Jira and Linear come through the same adapter, each with its own way to make a type, so adding a tracker adds one adapter and changes no play."; "Where the mapping is kept is our default: with the project's settings that the plays already read. The sources do not say where."; "It exists because a tracker does not always have these types: on 2026-10-25 Garura's own GitHub organization had no Epic type, so /shape-plan could not file an Epic as an Epic (#875)."

Every section is a list of discrete points. Acceptance is Given/When/Then, e.g. "Given a GitHub project whose organization has no Epic type, when initialize runs, then the brief lists the six types with their meanings and marks Epic as missing." The feature states the function's behavior ("It lists each needed type with its one-line meaning and says which are missing"), with no user-story form.

Parent gives one line: "Set up the tracker's work-item types (fn-881): finds the tracker the project uses and the types it has, makes each missing type after a typed yes, and records a stand-in where a type cannot be made." The feature adds its inputs and outputs, the mapping the plays read, the play-side stop rule ("the play stops with a plain message and points to `initialize`; it never files the item as some other type on its own"), the no-answer branch and six testable acceptance criteria.

What: "compares them with the types Garura's plays file ... After the product owner's typed yes, it makes each missing type and records what it made." Why: "on 2026-10-25 Garura's own GitHub organization had no Epic type, so /shape-plan could not file an Epic as an Epic (#875). Every project meets the same gap the first time a play writes to its tracker." Edges: "Filing epics, stories and other work items (/shape-plan and the other filing plays own them)." A cold reader can explain the what, why and edges from the doc alone; the only soft spot is "the same adapter", which reads as the tracker's adapter from context.
